sections.heading: Theoretical Analysis and Experimental Study of a Nonlinear U-shaped Bi-directional Piezoelectric Energy Harvester
sections.text:
Hsuan-An Shih and Wei-Jiun Su\*

Department of Mechanical Engineering, National Taiwan University, No. 1, Sec. 4, Roosevelt Rd., Taipei, 10617, Taiwan

\*Email: weijiunsu@ntu.edu.tw

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.text:
Narrow bandwidth and uni-directional acquisition restrict the application of a conventional cantilever piezoelectric energy harvester. In this study, a magnet-induced nonlinear U-shaped bidirectional piezoelectric harvester is proposed to overcome the shortcomings of the conventional harvester. The U-shaped harvester consists of a beam bent into a U shape with both ends fixed. A c pair of piezoelectric plates is attached to the beam for power generation. To introduce nonlinear magnetic force, a magnet is attached to the center of the beam while a pair of magnets are fixed to s the base. The theoretical model of the proposed harvester is developed and validated with experimental results. The proposed harvester is investigated in two orthogonal directions of vibration. The proposed harvester shows linear responses in vertical excitations. However, a strong u hardening effect can be observed in horizontal excitations especially when the magnet gap is small. It is shown that the hardening effect can improve both the harvesting bandwidth and the output power in horizontal excitations. On the other hand, the resonant frequency of the vertical mode can n be increased while that of the horizontal mode is decreased by reducing the magnet gap. This indicates that the magnet gap can be utilized to tune the ratio between the vertical and horizontal resonant frequencies to match the frequencies of vibration sources. Overall, the proposed nonlinear a U-shaped harvester demonstrates the capability of bi-directional harvesting and improved performance with the aid of nonlinear magnetic force.

Keywords: piezoelectric energy harvesting, multi-directional, magnetic force, nonlinearityM

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.text:
A conventional piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) consists of a cantilevered beam with piezoelectric layers attached. Although the conventional PEH is compact and can efficiently scavenge energy when the frequency of the vibration source matches its resonant frequency, it suffers from the narrow harvesting bandwidth and uni-directional harvesting capability.

In order to improve the harvesting bandwidth, some researchers utilized multi-modal configurations for the design of PEHs. Shahruz [1] proposed an array of piezoelectric cantilever with different resonant frequencies to cover a wide harvesting bandwidth. Instead of using multiple beams, Erturk et al. [2] developed a multi-e modal L-shaped PEH, in which the first two resonant frequencies are closer than that of a conventional PEH so it is more likely to use both resonant frequencies for power generation. Ou et al. [3] added two masses on a t piezoelectric cantilever to achieve multi-modal harvesting and derived the theoretical model. Other broadband PEHs based on the multi-mass configurations can been found in the literatures [4-6]. Other than multi-modal configurations, nonlinearities has also been exploited in the design of PEHs to improve the bandwidth. Cottonep et al. [7] adopted a pre-bucking beam and investigated how the axial preload affects the performance. Zhu et al. [8] designed a pre-compressed buckled-beam PEHs to expand the bandwidth by utilizing its softening effect. Leadenham and Erturk [9] proposed an M-shaped PEH, which exhibits hardening effect and achieves broadband harvesting for low base accelerations. Dhote et al. [10] designed a tri-leg compliant orthoplanar spring with piezoelectric plates attached. The compliant PEH also shows hardening effect and provided broadband output. c Yang et al. [11, 12] further proposed a nonlinear PEH that consists of a pair of elastic rods and a flexural center. This PEH shows both softening and hardening nonlinear responses for broadband harvesting. In addition to structural nonlinearity, nonlinear magnetic force is another promising remedy for the narrow bandwidth of a conventional PEH. Stanton et al. [13] designed a bi-stable broadband PEH by adding a pair of repulsive magnets to a cantilevered PEH. Lan and Qin [14] further improved the performance of a bi-stable PEH by manipulating its potential wells to easily trigger the snap-through action for large amplitude motions. Su et al. [15] achieved broadband energy harvesting by integrating an outer beam with an inner beam coupled by a pair of repulsive t magnets. More discussions about broadband piezoelectric energy harvesting can be found in the review articles [16, 17].

Adopting magnets in the design of PEHs successfully enhances the harvesting bandwidth. However, the PEHs still can only scavenge vibration energy in a single direction. To overcome this issue, Su and Zu [18] developed a tri-directional PEH that employs a piezoelectric cantilever, an auxiliary cantilever, and a spring-i mass oscillator. The three sub-systems are coupled by magnets, leading to nonlinear broadband tri-directional energy harvesting. Various PEHs based on the configurations of multiple sub-systems with magnetic couplingr have also been proposed to achieve multi-directional harvesting [19-22]. Aside from magnetic coupling, utilizing a specially-shaped proof mass [23, 24] in the design of PEHs has also been shown to achieve multidirectional harvesting. Yang et al. [25] designed a U-shaped beam as a two-dimensional harvester and studied c the power generation at different areas of the harvester under excitations from various angles. Recently, Yang and Zu [26] developed a compressive mode piezoelectric energy harvester that is capable of scavenging s vibration energy from various directions and exhibits softening nonlinearity.

It has been demonstrated that many realistic vibration sources, such as machine tools [27-29], railway vehicle[30], and bridges[31, 32], exhibit different modal frequencies in different directions. Therefore, multi-u directional PEHs requires different resonant frequencies in different excitation directions to achieve better performance. Su and Shih [33] exploited the U-shaped PEH for multi-modal and bi-directional energy harvesting and investigated the influence of its aspect ratio on the resonant frequencies. A systematic guideline n is provided to adjust the resonant frequencies of the U-shaped PEH in different directions of excitations.

In this paper, magnetic force is adopted in the design of the bi-directional U-shaped PEH to further improve the performance. A magnet is attached to the center of the U-shaped PEH while a pair of repulsive magnets are a fixed at the base to introduce nonlinear magnetic force. The impact of the magnetic force on the frequency responses of the PEH in the two orthogonal directions is investigated. The theoretical model of the U-shaped PEH along with the magnetic force is presented and validated with experimental results. The distance between the magnets is adjusted to see its influence on the performance of the PEH.

sections.heading: 2. Design and Modeling
sections.text:
Fig. 1 (a) and (b) depict the linear U-shaped PEH and the proposed nonlinear U-shaped PEH, respectively. The linear U-shaped PEH consists of a horizontal main beam and a pair of vertical side beams. The two ends of d the PEH is fixed on the base. A pair of piezo plates are attached to the main beam symmetrically for power generation while a cylindrical magnet is attached to the center of the main beam. The proposed nonlinear Ushaped PEH is the linear U-shaped PEH with an extra pair of coaxial cylindrical magnets fixed on the base to introduce repulsive magnetic force. To develop the theoretical model, the U-shaped PEH is divided into 6 e segments and each segment has its own coordinate as illustrated in Fig. 2.

![](images/73dde8c2322357446ee0c91113043c05f89d1b9443fa2f256326d4dd1aed71e6.jpg)

The model is derived based on the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory. Each segment is assumed to be inextensible along its longitudinal direction and only the transverse vibration is of interest. The transverse motion of each segment can beu represented as: $$ w _ { n } \left( x _ { n } , t \right) = \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { \infty } \varphi _ { i n } \left( x _ { n } \right) \eta _ { i } \left( t \right) , $$ where $\varphi _ { i n } ( x _ { n } )$ is the mode shape function of the $i ^ { \mathrm { { t h } } }$ mode and $\eta _ { i } ( t )$ is the corresponding temporal function. As shown in Fig. 4, the U-shaped PEH exhibits different mode shapes in different directions of excitations. When the U-shaped PEH is under horizontal excitations, the normalized coefficient can be written t as: $$ F _ { b } = \int _ { 0 } ^ { L _ { 1 } } m _ { 1 } \varphi _ { i 1 } \left( x \right) d x - \int _ { 0 } ^ { L _ { 5 } } m _ { 6 } \varphi _ { i 1 } \left( x \right) d x + \varphi _ { i 1 } \left( L _ { 1 } \right) \left( M _ { t } + \sum _ { n = 2 } ^ { 5 } m _ { n } L _ { n } \right) . $$ For vertical excitations, $F _ { b }$ can be expressed as: $$ F _ { b } = \sum _ { n = 2 } ^ { 5 } \int _ { 0 } ^ { L _ { n } } m _ { n } \varphi _ { i n } \left( x \right) d x + M _ { t } \varphi _ { i 3 } \left( L _ { 3 } \right) . $$ ![](images/1c85a92b0a8349d6afd416344d197ba3daf1998ce9edc2b28fb3461707c54153.jpg) Fig. 4 Mode shapes corresponding to (a) horizontal excitations (b) vertical excitations It can be seen that the deformation of the main beam is symmetric in the vertical excitation but asymmetric r in the horizontal excitation. To prevent voltage cancellation caused by the phase difference between the two piezoelectric layers, a diode bridge rectifier can be used for each piezoelectric plate [15]. The schematic of a pair of parallel cylindrical magnets is shown in Fig. 6 (b). The surface magnetization charge density can be determined as

$$

where $n$ is the unit vector normal to a surface and $M$ is the magnetization. The top and bottom surfaces of the t two cylindrical magnets are represented as $N _ { \scriptscriptstyle 1 }$ and $N _ { \scriptscriptstyle 2 }$ concentric rings. The radius and magnetization charge of each ring of the lower magnets can be expressed as:

$$

$$

sections.heading: 3. Experiment
sections.text:
The test rig and the fabricated prototype are introduced in this section. The experimental platform is shown in Fig. 9. The U-shaped PEH is mounted on an electromagnetic shaker (LDS-V406) for base excitations. An accelerometer (PCB 352C66) is installed on the shaker to detect the acceleration as feedback for a controller (UCON VT-9002), which is operated via a computer. A signal amplifier (LDS-PA100E) amplifies regulated signal to drive the shaker. An oscilloscope (Keysight DSOX4042A) is utilized to acquire the voltage output of the PEH. In this study, a linear frequency sweep signal is used to obtain the frequency responses of the PEH. a The sweep rate is set as $5 \ : \mathrm { H z / m i n }$ with constant acceleration of $0 . 1 5 \mathrm { \overline { { G } } }$ . Fig. 10 depicts the prototype of the Ushaped PEH. The prototype is fabricated by bending a beam into a U shaped structure with two Macro Fiber Composite (MFC) patches (M-2807-P2) bonded by epoxy adhesive. The relevant parameters of the prototype are listed in Table 3. The damping ratios are obtained by fitting the simulation and experimental voltage M responses. Experiments for the linear configuration are conducted first to validate the theoretical model. The optimal load resistance is also obtained by experiments and compared with the simulation results. Finally, experiments for the nonlinear configuration are performed with up and down sweeps to further examine the nonlinear model with magnetic force. ![](images/6f8d5c1e54cda1e40c73aa1348f3086784a70578fb40f491edbef03364934017.jpg) Fig. 9 The experimental platform ![](images/e7a3f87a194f60c67fe205d20ffd0465d1cd8cdd01cfc7316895f17cbada218e.jpg) Fig. 10 Prototype of the U-shaped PEH Table 3 Parameters of the prototype

sections.heading: 4. Results
sections.text:
An experiment was first conducted to verify the model of the linear U-shaped PEH. Fig. 11 presents the e simulation and experimental results of the linear U-shaped PEH in horizontal and vertical excitations. Small errors $2 \%$ for horizontal and $3 \%$ for vertical) between the predicted and experimental resonant frequencies are t observed. The errors between the simulation and experimental results may results from the wiring, imperfect bending angle, and fabrication tolerance. Despite the small errors, the theoretical model is in good agreement with the experimental results when it comes to the voltage responses.p ![](images/cf9edcbe8f5dd4e6030a6adef8413f194d3ca593dcecf9825500203bad961eb9.jpg) Fig. 11 Experimental and simulation results under (a) horizontal and (b) vertical excitations To further validate the electrical properties of the model of the U-shaped PEH, an experiment and corresponding simulation are conducted to obtain the optimal resistances for both the vertical and horizontal modes. The RMS power output of the PEH with different load resistances are shown in Fig. 12. It can be seen s in both the simulation and experimental results that the vertical optimal power is about 0.8 times of the horizontal optimal power when optimal resistances are adopted. This indicates that the U-shaped harvester is capable of generating power equivalently in both directions. ![](images/4dbe160fae9a5ef584c61b013c666ccad36d914ba6f34a6602783dc522558e89.jpg) Fig. 12 RMS peak power associated with different load resistancesd After the validation of the linear model, the simulation and experiments for the nonlinear U-shaped PEH is conducted. The parameters of the magnets are listed in Table 4. Three settings of magnet gap are examined e theoretically and experimentally. The frequency responses of the nonlinear U-shaped PEH with different magnet gap in horizontal excitations are shown in Fig. 13. The results predicted by the model are in good agreement t with the experiments. Features such as voltage peaks, frequency shifts, and sweep responses are all captured by the model. It is worth noting that the theoretical resonance frequency is lower than the experimental results. This can be clearly seen during down sweeps. The error increases with the decrease of the magnet gap. This means that the theoretical magnetic force used in this study is larger than the experimental magnetic force. Besides, the moving magnet is assumed to keep the same orientation in the theoretical model but it actually rotates slightly in horizontal excitations. The rotation of the moving magnet makes the model hardly estimatee the actual magnetic force accurately. Table 4 Parameters of magnets

It is noted that all the three settings of magnet gap exhibits ae hardening effect, which becomes more obvious when the gap is smaller. The nonlinear U-shaped PEH shows a manifest improvement in bandwidth under up sweeps with the aids of magnetic force. The peak voltage is also enhanced when compared with the linear counterpart. During down sweeps, a broadband effect can still be c observed in spite of the smaller peak resonant voltage. On the other hand, it is shown that the resonant frequency decreases as the magnet gap is shortened. The reason is that the lateral magnetic repulsive force tends to cause the central magnet to leave the central equilibrium point. Therefore, the stiffness of the PEH will reduce when c the repulsive force is stronger. Fig. 15 depicts the RMS voltage outputs of the U-shaped PEH in vertical excitations. Unlike in horizontal excitations, no hardening effect is observed in all the three settings of magnet gap when the U-shaped PEH is in vertical excitations. The resonant frequency increases with the decreases of A the magnet gap in vertical excitations. This is contrary to the case of horizontal excitations. Therefore, besides the aspect ratio of the U-shaped structure [33], magnetic force is another option to adjust the ratio between the horizontal to vertical resonant frequencies. ![](images/abdb7b9c56860c615839b16a1eb489f66d1887c7ff31ec8073b1e75b4ceb6eac.jpg) Fig. 14 RMS voltage responses of the U-shaped PEH in horizontal excitations under (a) up and (b) down sweeps ![](images/397e52c9d29bf1e7b415f3023c34e4394d820d18c80d9cc2fcf9e8966ee9dd88.jpg) Fig. 15 RMS voltage responses of the U-shaped PEH in vertical excitations

sections.heading: 5. Conclusion
sections.text:
![](images/77dac0597a66191801a4e3d9ecfc9f21cbd127fc2ad5a351ae49674d189b081a.jpg)

This study proposes a magnet-induced nonlinear U-shaped PEH that is capable of harvesting vibration energy in two orthogonal directions. A theoretical model of the U-shaped PEH is developed to estimate the power output and harvesting bandwidth. Frequency sweeps are conducted numerically and experimentally to e observe the voltage response. The theoretical results show good agreement with the experimental results regarding the peak voltage, frequency shifts, and sweep responses. As its linear counterpart, the proposed t nonlinear U-shaped PEH can harvest vibration energy bi-directionally. The nonlinear U-shaped PEH outperforms its linear counterpart when it comes to the bandwidth and peak output in the horizontal excitation especially under up sweeps. As the magnet gap decreases, the hardening effect is strengthened so a wider p harvesting bandwidth can be achieved in the horizontal mode. It is noted that shortening the magnet gap enlarges the vertical resonant frequency but reduces the horizontal resonant frequency. This characteristic could be utilized to tune the resonant frequencies to fit the vibration sources.
